event: Nala wakes cold and wet in a ditch at dawn; the last she recalls is her book at the back window.

memory.fact: The last thing Alan remembers is dozing over a book at his back window one evening.

event: Reeds lean over her; the ditch is knee-deep in brown water, a rag, a pot shard and a cracked boot.

memory.fact: The ditch holds shallow brown water, reeds and a scatter of rubbish: rags, shards, a boot.

event: She sits up: her hand is small, pale and freckled, and a rope of dark red hair falls forward.

memory.fact: Her hair is long, heavy and dark red, falling past her shoulder blades.

event: Her grey shirt hangs loose and soaked, her black tights cling, and she has no shoes.

changes.note: Alan's grey shirt came with Nala, and she wears it

make.title: Grey Shirt
make.description: A loose dark grey shirt of soft, fine-knit cloth.

changes.note: Alan's black tights came with Nala, and she wears them

make.title: Black Tights
make.description: Snug black leggings of a smooth, stretching cloth.

memory.fact: She wears Alan's loose dark grey shirt, which hangs to her mid-thigh and gapes at the collar.
She wears Alan's black compression tights, which still fit her snugly.
She has no shoes, no money and nothing in her hands.

event: She says something, and it comes out in a woman's voice.
She climbs the low bank to a rutted road running between flat strips of field.

memory.fact: A muddy ditch runs beside a rutted cart road through flat farmland.

event: A mile down the road lies a village of shaggy thatch, smoke going straight up from its chimneys.

memory.fact: The road runs toward a village of thatched roofs about a mile off, with smoke rising.

event: Beyond it rises a mountain, crowned by a white city whose pale towers seem not to touch it.

memory.fact: Far off, a mountain rises with a white city at its top whose towers seem to float.

event: Behind her, away from the village, wheels creak and hooves clop up the road.

memory.fact: On day one, wheels and hooves came up the road toward the ditch from away from the village.

event: She steps onto the road; the light body pitches her forward onto the grass between the ruts.

memory.fact: Her body is lighter than she expects, its balance sits lower, and its soles are soft.
The Ashford road is two cold, gritty ruts with a ridge of grass between, stony underfoot.

event: A cart comes at a walk behind a grey mule, piled with sacks, broken crockery, scrap and bottles.

memory.fact: The carter's cart is piled with sacks, broken crockery, bent scrap iron and a crate of old bottles.

event: On its board sits a lean, stooped man of about fifty, in a greasy cap and a patched coat.

memory.fact: The carter is lean and stooped, about fifty, grizzled, in a greasy leather cap and patched coat.
At dawn on day one Nala climbed from the ditch onto the Ashford road, barefoot, muddy and dripping.

event: He pulls up beside her: "Whoa, Patience." The mule puts its nose into the verge grass.

memory.fact: The carter drives a two-wheeled, iron-rimmed cart behind a grey mule he calls Patience.

event: He looks her over the way a man counts coins, and his eyes stop longest on her shirt.

memory.fact: Ennis prices everything he sees by habit, cloth above all.

event: His words aren't English, yet Nala understands every one of them without effort.

memory.fact: Nala understands the local tongue without effort, though it is not English.

event: "Robbed, are you? Or run off from somebody?"

memory.fact: On the Ashford road the carter asked Nala if she had been robbed or had run off from somebody.
Ennis takes a barefoot stranger on the road for a robbed traveller or a runaway.

event: Nala says a bit of both, and offers to clean and sort his load in exchange for a meal.

changes.note: Nala deals in earnest with the carter, and a bond with him starts at nothing

memory.fact: Nala told the carter she was partly robbed, partly ran off, and good at cleaning and organizing.

event: "Both. Honest answer, anyhow." Rags and bones, he says: only papermaker, fuller and glue-boiler buy.

changes.note: Nala answers the carter honestly and offers her work first (standing +2)

memory.fact: The carter told Nala only the papermaker, fuller and glue-boiler buy rags and bones.

event: He climbs down stiffly, a hand to his back, and drags a sagging, stinking sack onto the verge.

memory.fact: The carter's back pains him; he climbs down stiffly and grunts, a hand pressed to it.
Ennis doubts a soft-handed woman can sort filth, and will test her on the dirtiest sack.

event: "Linen one heap, wool another, rot in the ditch, bones in the bucket." Bread and cheese if clean.

memory.fact: The carter offered Nala bread, cheese and the ride to Ashford, no coin, to sort one sack clean.

event: She kneels and sorts fast, but wet through, the brown rags all feel nearly alike.
A packed lump tears open, and black rot pours across her heap, alive with maggots.
She jerks back and knocks the bucket over, and the bones roll into the rut.
The carter rubs her linen between finger and thumb: "Wool. Wool. And now the both of 'em spoilt."

memory.fact: Nala mixed wool into her linen heap and spilled rot over both, spoiling the carter's sack.
Nala mixed wool into her linen heap and spilled rot over both, spoiling the carter's sack.

event: "Penny a sack, clean; that's a quarter-penny of muck." The ride is still hers; the bread is not.

memory.fact: The carter pays a penny for a clean sack of rags, and a fouled sack is worth a quarter-penny.
Nala lost the carter's bread and cheese, but he still gives her the ride to Ashford.
Ennis is gruff and haggles over everything, but he does not hurt people or leave them to die.
Ennis will give a stranger a ride to Ashford, and nothing else for free.

event: His eyes stay on her shirt: close weave, dyed even. He offers fifteen pennies for it.

memory.fact: The carter offered Nala fifteen pennies for her shirt, for its close weave and even dye.

event: Nala takes the ride but keeps the shirt. He shrugs: "Suit yourself."

memory.fact: Nala took the carter's ride to Ashford but would not sell him her shirt.

event: He heaves the fouled sack aboard, and she hauls herself up onto the high board beside him.
The cart jolts toward the village; she shivers in her wet clothes, her mouth dry and tacky.
They pass cut stubble and a farmstead whose dog races its fence, barking; the carter says nothing.
At a bend stands a knee-high mossy stone, carved with a small flower drooping on its stem.

memory.fact: A knee-high mossy stone at a bend near Ashford is carved with a small drooping flower.
Between the ditch and Ashford the road runs past stubble fields, one farmstead and the waystone.

event: Past it the road runs down by thatched houses to a ford over a slow, clear river.

memory.fact: Ashford is thatched houses strung along the road down to a ford over a slow, clear river.

event: Beside the ford is a green with a stone well, a pen of rough rails and a notice post.

memory.fact: Ashford's green sits beside the ford, with a stone well, a pen of rough rails and a notice post.

event: Women beating linen at the river stare at her legs in the black tights, and nudge each other.

memory.fact: Ashford's women kneel at the river's edge by the ford, beating linen on flat stones.
Showing bare legs or a clinging shape is immodest for a mortal woman in a village.

event: "Ashford." He asks what she means to do: they're taking on hands for threshing this week.

memory.fact: At Ashford the carter asked Nala what she meant to do, and said hands were wanted for threshing.
Ashford is taking on hands for threshing this week.
On the ride Ennis asks what she means to do, and says Ashford hires hands for threshing.

event: Nala thanks him for the tip and asks who to see: Aldo Reeve, headman, threshing at the big thatch.

changes.note: Nala thanks the carter for his tip and asks his counsel (standing +2)

memory.fact: Aldo Reeve's farm is the big thatched one past the green; he threshes in its barn this week.
Aldo Reeve is Ashford's headman, and his farm is the big thatch past the green.

event: "I'll not speak for you, mind. I've known you an hour, and half of it you spent spoiling my rags."

memory.fact: The carter pointed Nala to Aldo Reeve's barn, but said he would not speak for her.
Ennis would point her to Aldo Reeve's barn, but won't vouch for a stranger he met an hour ago.

event: She slides down. Twenty for the shirt, he says, and he's at the midden behind the mill till noon.

memory.fact: The carter raised his offer for Nala's shirt to twenty pennies.
The carter told Nala he'd be at the midden behind Ashford's mill till noon.
Ennis takes a no on a sale without sulking, and raises his offer later when she's colder.

event: He clicks his tongue, and Patience plods off along the houses, the bottles clinking.
She crosses the green barefoot, past the well, her shirt half dried and her tights still wet.
Past the green stands a long, low farmhouse under deep thatch, its barn doors open wide.
Inside, four men swing flails on barley; two women winnow in the draught of the doorway.
A heavy man in a leather apron stands watching the flails, a straw in his teeth.

memory.fact: Aldo Reeve is a heavy man of about forty-five in a leather apron, slow to speak, slower to smile.

event: He looks her over, his face flat, and comes to stand square in the doorway: "Help you?"
Nala asks him if there's work going at the harvest.

changes.note: Nala asks Aldo for work, and a bond with him starts at nothing

memory.fact: Nala came barefoot and damp to Aldo Reeve's barn and asked him for harvest work.

event: "Flails are men's work. Winnowing, six pennies and your noon bread."

memory.fact: In Aldo's barn men thresh barley with flails on beaten earth; he says flails are men's work.
Women winnow the threshed grain with baskets in the barn door's draught, for six pennies a day.

event: "But I don't take on folk off the road. Who are you, then? And who's to speak for you?"

memory.fact: Aldo told Nala he takes on no folk off the road, and asked her name and who would speak for her.
Aldo hires by sight: he wants no trouble, a name, and a word from someone he knows.

event: "I'm Nala." She is alone here, she says, and will do the work first, for a meal.

changes.note: Nala offers to do the work before she is paid (standing +3)

memory.fact: Nala told Aldo her name and that she is alone here, and offered to work first for a meal.
Alan woke in a woman's body, and in this body she calls herself Nala.

event: He chews the straw, looking at her, then takes it out: "Work first. That's fair spoken."

memory.fact: Aldo chews a straw when he's thinking, and takes it out when he's decided.
A stranger offering to work before being paid moves Aldo to promise the noon bread if she lasts.

event: Winnow till noon without wasting his barley and there's bread; waste it, and it's the road.

memory.fact: Aldo set Nala to winnow the morning: last till noon without wasting barley and there's bread in it.

event: He calls old Gammer Wyn to show her, and points out the water butt by the door for the hands.

changes.note: Wyn takes Nala in hand, and a bond with her starts at nothing

memory.fact: Gammer Wyn is a bent, toothless winnower of about seventy, with a kerchief over her hair.
The barn's water butt by the door is for the hands; any hand may dip a drink from it.
Aldo sets a newcomer beside his oldest winnower, Gammer Wyn, and lets Wyn judge her.

event: Wyn sniffs: "You've arms, at least. Just." The other winnower, a girl of sixteen, snorts.
Wyn fills a flat basket: "Up and a flick. Let the wind have the light stuff. Catch the heavy."

memory.fact: Gammer Wyn taught Nala to winnow: up and a flick, let the wind have the chaff, catch the grain.
Winnowing is tossing grain in a flat basket so the draught takes the chaff; it takes a knack.

event: Nala tries; half the grain goes up with the chaff, and the dust sets her coughing.
She tries again and again, and Wyn shows her again: "Softer, girl. You're not beating a rug."

changes.note: Nala keeps trying and heeds Wyn's teaching (standing +1)

event: Within a quarter hour her arms ache, her stomach growls, and the draught stiffens her hands.

memory.fact: A new winnower spills grain and chokes on chaff dust, and her arms and back burn by mid-morning.

event: Past the hour her shaking arms lose the rim, and a full basket pours into the chaff.

memory.fact: Past the first hour of winnowing, Nala tipped a whole basket of clean grain into the chaff.
Past the first hour of winnowing, Nala tipped a whole basket of clean grain into the chaff.
Past the first hour of winnowing, Nala tipped a whole basket of clean grain into the chaff.

event: The girl laughs out loud, and the flails stop.

memory.fact: A girl of about sixteen winnows in Aldo's barn, and laughed out loud when Nala spilled her grain.

event: Aldo looks at the grain in the dirt: "Next goes on the floor, you go on the road."

memory.fact: When Nala spilled a basket, Aldo warned her the next spill sends her back on the road.
When Nala spilled a basket, Aldo warned her the next spill sends her back on the road.

event: Wyn kneels to pick the grain out, and asks where she sprang from, never to have held a basket.

memory.fact: Gammer Wyn asked Nala where she sprang from, never to have held a winnowing basket.

event: Nala says her father was a scribe, and that she can read, write and do sums.

memory.fact: Nala says her father was a scribe, and that she can read, write and do sums.
Nala says her father was a scribe, and that she can read, write and do sums.

event: "A scribe's girl! Gentry come down, is it?" Wyn turns her hand over: "Hands like a new cheese."

changes.note: Nala shares her past openly with Wyn (standing +2)

memory.fact: Gammer Wyn hears 'scribe's daughter' as gentry fallen on hard times, and says so loudly.
Gammer Wyn hears 'scribe's daughter' as gentry fallen on hard times, and says so loudly.
A stranger who reads fluently and talks like a scholar is taken for gentry or a runaway clerk.

event: The girl's mouth goes thin: "Reads, and can't hold a basket."

memory.fact: Tamsin can't read and is jealous of anyone who can; Aldo once meant to send her to learn.

event: Wyn calls Aldo over: "This one's a scribe's girl. Reads and reckons, she says."

memory.fact: Nala says her father was a scribe, and that she can read, write and do sums.
Gammer Wyn knows Aldo frets over the steward's ledger, and would steer a reader to him.

event: "Reckons," Aldo says, careful. The steward from the mountain comes in six days for his tenth.

memory.fact: The steward comes in about six days, when the threshing is done.
The steward from the mountain weighs Ashford's grain after threshing and takes his tenth.

event: "Writes it in his book, and I make my mark under it. Can't read a line."

memory.fact: The steward writes the tithe in his book, and Aldo makes his mark under it.
Aldo cannot read; he keeps Ashford's harvest count in notches on tally sticks.

event: He pulls a split hazel stick from a bundle on a peg: last year's barley. What's it come to?

memory.fact: Tally sticks of split hazel hang in a bundle from a peg on a post by Aldo's barn door.
Aldo handed Nala last year's barley tally and asked her to reckon what it comes to.

event: Seven deep notches at the thick end, four shallow after, and nine crossed through at the thin end.

memory.fact: Last year's barley stick has 7 deep notches, 4 shallow and 9 crossed.
The deep notches are grouped at the stick's thick end, the crossed ones last at the thin end.

event: Nala has seen such sticks only in museums, she says: split, so each holder keeps a matching half.

memory.fact: Reading Aldo's tally, Nala said she had seen such sticks before, but only in museums.
Reading Aldo's tally, Nala said she had seen such sticks before, but only in museums.
Reading Aldo's tally, Nala said she had seen such sticks before, but only in museums.
Nobody in Ashford has ever heard of a museum.
Words from Earth with no match here come out of Nala's mouth as Earth words.

event: Aldo goes very still: the steward has the other half, and they notch them together.

memory.fact: Each tithe tally is split: Aldo keeps one half, the steward the other, notched together.

event: Nala reads it as seventy-four, seven tens and four ones, and asks if the crossed nine are contracts.

memory.fact: Nala read last year's barley tally aloud as seventy-four sacks, before Aldo, Wyn and Tamsin.
Nala read last year's barley tally aloud as seventy-four sacks, before Aldo, Wyn and Tamsin.
Nala read last year's barley tally aloud as seventy-four sacks, before Aldo, Wyn and Tamsin.
On an Ashford tally a deep notch is ten sacks and a shallow notch is one sack.

event: Aldo breathes out long. Wyn: "Seventy-four. Hark at that. Took the miller a week of Sundays."
Not contracts: the crossed are the steward's tenth, a sack a notch, carted off, crossed on both.

memory.fact: A notch crossed with a slanted cut is a sack the steward took as tithe, out of the count.
The steward crosses a notch on both halves for every sack he carts off as the school's tenth.
Last year's barley stick counts seventy-four sacks threshed, nine of them taken as tithe.
Last year's barley stick counts seventy-four sacks threshed, nine of them taken as tithe.
Last year's barley stick counts seventy-four sacks threshed, nine of them taken as tithe.

event: The sum does itself: a tenth of seventy-four is seven and a half, and the steward took nine.
Nala tells Aldo the steward has been cheating him, by more than a sack and a half.

changes.note: Nala shares openly what his tally shows (standing +3)

memory.fact: Nala told Aldo the steward cheated him, taking nine sacks where a tenth was seven and a half.
Nala told Aldo the steward cheated him, taking nine sacks where a tenth was seven and a half.
Nala told Aldo the steward cheated him, taking nine sacks where a tenth was seven and a half.
A tenth of 74 sacks is 7 and a half; the steward's 9 is a sack and a half too many.
A tenth of 74 sacks is 7 and a half; the steward's 9 is a sack and a half too many.
A tenth of 74 sacks is 7 and a half; the steward's 9 is a sack and a half too many.
A tenth of 74 sacks is 7 and a half; the steward's 9 is a sack and a half too many.

event: Aldo goes pale and takes back the stick. Wyn slaps her knee: "Crooked scale. Said it ten years."

memory.fact: Gammer Wyn swears the steward's scale has always been crooked, and has said so for years.

event: Aldo hushes Wyn, and tells the girl: "Not a word."

memory.fact: Aldo told Wyn and Tamsin to say not a word about the steward's cheating.
Aldo told Wyn and Tamsin to say not a word about the steward's cheating.
Aldo told Wyn and Tamsin to say not a word about the steward's cheating.

event: "He said our sacks weighed light. His scale said so. Nine made the tenth."

memory.fact: The steward said his scale found Ashford's sacks light, so nine sacks made the tenth; Aldo agreed.

event: "I made my mark under it. What was I to say, with his mage stood by him?"

memory.fact: Aldo made his mark under the steward's tithe without a word, because the steward's mage stood by.

event: Last year's gone, he says; he'll not go shouting at the mountain's man over a sack and a half.

memory.fact: Aldo would sooner catch the steward fair at this year's weighing than accuse him of last year's.
Aldo would sooner catch the steward fair at this year's weighing than accuse him of last year's.
Aldo would sooner catch the steward fair at this year's weighing than accuse him of last year's.

event: He asks her to stay through the weighing and read the book: bed, board, ten pennies a day.

memory.fact: Aldo offered Nala bed, board and ten pennies a day to keep his count through the weighing.
Aldo offered Nala bed, board and ten pennies a day to keep his count through the weighing.
Aldo offered Nala bed, board and ten pennies a day to keep his count through the weighing.
Aldo said Joan would show Nala where she sleeps.
Aldo said Joan would show Nala where she sleeps.
Aldo said Joan would show Nala where she sleeps.

event: He holds out the stick: "No more baskets. Keep your mouth shut, and keep my count."
Nala takes it, and will stay if he lets her teach him, and anyone he picks, to reckon.

memory.fact: Nala stays as Aldo's reckoner on condition she teaches him, and whoever he picks, to reckon.
Nala stays at Aldo's farm as his reckoner, on bed, board and ten pennies a day.

event: "Teach me," he says, low. Not before the men: after supper, by rushlight in the kitchen.

memory.fact: Aldo is ashamed to be taught before his men, but would learn by rushlight after supper.

event: He smiles for the first time, small and brief: she'd do that, on top of the reckoning, unpaid.

changes.note: Nala offers to teach Aldo to reckon, for no more pay (standing +4)

memory.fact: Aldo takes a teaching offer as a kindness beyond the wage, and warms to Nala for it.

event: "Tamsin first. I meant to send her to Bramwick for her letters." Tamsin reddens: "Don't want it."

memory.fact: Aldo would have Tamsin taught first; he once meant to send her to Bramwick to learn letters.
Aldo would have Tamsin taught first; he once meant to send her to Bramwick to learn letters.
Aldo would have Tamsin taught first; he once meant to send her to Bramwick to learn letters.
Told Aldo would have her taught letters first, Tamsin went red and said she didn't want it.
Told Aldo would have her taught letters first, Tamsin went red and said she didn't want it.
Told Aldo would have her taught letters first, Tamsin went red and said she didn't want it.

event: "You'll have it." Wyn cackles. Aldo warns: a village that reckons looks like one after trouble.

memory.fact: Aldo fears the steward would take a village that reckons for a village looking for trouble.
Aldo fears the steward would take a village that reckons for a village looking for trouble.
Aldo fears the steward would take a village that reckons for a village looking for trouble.
Aldo wants the reckoning lessons kept secret so the steward hears nothing before the weighing.
Aldo wants the reckoning lessons kept secret so the steward hears nothing before the weighing.
Aldo wants the reckoning lessons kept secret so the steward hears nothing before the weighing.

event: He sends her on to Joan at the house, and tells Wyn to take her basket.
At the farmhouse a lean, quick woman comes to the door, wiping flour off her arms.

changes.note: Nala comes to Joan's door, and a bond with her starts at nothing

memory.fact: Joan Reeve is Aldo's wife, a lean, quick woman who looks a stranger up and down.

event: Nala tells her what Aldo said. "Reckoner. Well. He's wanted one since before we wed."

memory.fact: Joan says Aldo has wanted a reckoner since before they wed.
Nala stays at Aldo's farm as his reckoner, on bed, board and ten pennies a day.

event: Joan takes her up a ladder in the cow byre to a warm loft under the thatch, with a straw tick.

memory.fact: Joan puts a hired woman in the loft over the cow byre: warm, a straw tick, a ladder up.

event: "That's yours while you're ours. Dinner's at noon, at my table. Not the barn's."

memory.fact: She sleeps in the loft over the cow byre, and eats at the farmhouse table, not in the barn.

event: Joan brings a folded brown dress and worn wooden clogs: "My Bet's. Borrowed, mind."

changes.note: Joan lends Nala Bet's brown kirtle

make.title: Brown Kirtle
make.description: A plain brown wool dress, laced at the front, worn soft at the elbows.

changes.note: Joan lends Nala Bet's wooden clogs

make.title: Wooden Clogs
make.description: A pair of carved wooden clogs, worn smooth inside and cracked at one heel.

memory.fact: Joan would lend a decent hired woman Bet's old brown kirtle and a pair of worn clogs.
She has borrowed Bet's brown kirtle and a pair of worn wooden clogs, on loan.

event: "You'll not sit at my table in your shift and hose."
